agent.name: Emerging Technology Diffusion Agent
agent.specialty: Diffusion stage, mechanisms and bounded timing implications

analytical_question: What can the supplied evidence establish about agentic-AI diffusion versus chart-review diffusion, mechanisms, and the timing/peer implications for the hypothetical firm?
general_et_finding: Provisional assessment: agentic AI has demonstrable cross-functional organizational scaling among surveyed respondents, but its Rogers stage in a defined population cannot be assigned. S1 reports 40% for a large-revenue respondent subgroup and 22% for a smaller one; these are not innovation-specific adopter quantiles. Knowledge and persuasion are visible through survey and vendor discussion; decision, implementation and confirmation for individual firms are not tracked. Change agents may include platform vendors and internal AI champions; opinion leaders may include peer analysts and risk owners. Their actual influence is unmeasured.
application_finding: The chart-to-source review application has no measured installed base, so provisional stage is pre-confirmation/exploratory, not a demonstrated early-majority application. Rogers attributes, as hypotheses: relative advantage—possible reduced review effort, unmeasured; compatibility—plausible fit to approved BI tables and human sign-off; complexity—SQL permissions, source lineage and error propagation; trialability—high for synthetic read-only examples; observability—potentially high through auditable discrepancy logs, but no observed outcomes. Knowledge and persuasion are plausible; local decision is limited to study, with implementation and confirmation absent. Analyst champions could demonstrate workflows; independent report owners and security staff may inhibit unsupported claims.
organization_specific_finding: For this constructed conservative mid-sized financial-services firm, approved synthetic/public-data sandbox access enables a four-week learning exercise, not production use. Production data and external production-model approval are absent; analyst ownership remains. Relative advantage, safety and peer position remain unknown. A more aggressive firm might investigate sooner with greater tolerated uncertainty, but would not thereby change S1/S2 denominators or establish a different general diffusion stage. Financial reporting consequences raise the burden of traceability, making production timing contingent on evidence and permissions.

evidence.claim: Agent scaling in at least one function: 40% among respondents in report-defined large-revenue group versus 27% previous survey; smaller group 22%.
evidence.source_or_reference: S1: McKinsey, The state of AI in 2026, agent-use discussion/Exhibit 2
evidence.notes: 1,719 respondents across 97 nations; neither firm census nor chart-review application count.

evidence.claim: Finance and Insurance AI use in any business function 33.9%, versus national 19.8%.
evidence.source_or_reference: S2: US Census, Large Firms With at Least 20 Employees Biggest AI Users
evidence.notes: Not agent scaling; November 2025 wording break; cannot infer chart-agent penetration.

evidence.claim: Rogers categories, five attributes, diffusion process, influence actors, 16% heuristic.
evidence.source_or_reference: C1: ET Module 6 The Diffusion of Emerging Technologies FA25, slides 18-29, 32-35, 40-54, 58-63
evidence.notes: Heuristics are not measurements of this use case or peer social system.

evidence.claim: Model-directed tools create flexible multi-step behavior but entail complexity, costs and compounding-error risk.
evidence.notes: Design mechanism, not independent diffusion or performance evidence.

evidence.claim: MCP specifies model-to-tool connectivity with consent/security considerations.
evidence.notes: Potential ecosystem accelerator, not proof of adoption or compatibility.

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: S1 scaling is any function and respondent-defined revenue groups; the hypothetical firm cannot be mapped to either group without revenue.
S2 measures any AI use and contains a questionnaire wording change; it is neither a chart-agent denominator nor current October adoption.
No application-specific peer installed base, measured local error rate, time savings, or organizational implementation data exist.
confidence_and_uncertainty: Moderate confidence that some agentic AI scales across surveyed organizations; low confidence in a Rogers label, comparable-peer position, or chart-review adoption stage. Factor ratings and actor roles are analytical hypotheses, not field observations.
value_opportunity_implication: A bounded synthetic study can expose workflow feasibility and measurable review-effort hypotheses without implying realized ROI. Potential ecosystem acceleration comes from tool standards (S4) and vendor guidance (S3), tempered by integration and accountability burdens.
risk_governance_implication: Maintain read-only access, synthetic/public data, correction-note drafts and human sign-off. Security and report owners should verify source traceability and prevent unauthorized production access. Vendor advocacy is persuasion evidence, not a substitute for validation.
recommendation_management_implication: Diffusion/timing implication only: use the four-week window to collect application-specific signals; reassess quarterly over 12 months. The course 16% chasm heuristic requires a common adoption population and comparable adoption measure, neither provided. Do not derive an irreversible crossing or urgent rollout from mixed survey rates; no full adoption decision is made.
change_monitoring_triggers: Four-week results: reproducible chart/source comparison, discrepancy accuracy, traceability and analyst-time measurements on synthetic cases.
Quarterly: comparable financial-firm chart-review deployments with defined denominator and sustained use.
Changes in security permission, production-data approval, tool interoperability or observed error patterns.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: Abstain from Rogers adopter-category quantile, exact chasm crossing date, irreversible diffusion and peer ranking.
Obtain comparison-set definition, active chart-review installations and longitudinal adoption evidence; local controlled-study outcomes.
